title: Cassini's 1665 spot probably wasn't the Great Red Spot
description:
In 1665, Giovanni Cassini saw a dark oval on Jupiter, at the latitude of today's Great Red Spot. Astronomers kept reporting his spot until 1713. Then, for about 118 years, it appears in no surviving observation. The storm we call the Great Red Spot first shows up in drawings in 1831, as a light 'Hollow' in a cloud belt; it turned reddish only in the 1870s. Cassini's spot was only a third to a half as long as the Great Red Spot was in 1879. To be the same storm, it would have had to grow steadily, by about 160 km a year, for 166 years without anyone seeing it, and no storm on Jupiter has ever been seen to grow like that. So the Great Red Spot has been on record since 1831, and Cassini's spot was most likely a different storm that disappeared.

Source:
- Sánchez-Lavega et al. 2024, "The Origin of Jupiter's Great Red Spot", Geophysical Research Letters 51(12), e2024GL108993. doi:10.1029/2024GL108993

Narration: Kokoro-82M synthetic voice. Illustrated animation; the planet and the spots on it are not to scale.
